about.text: The sour buttermilk of Sudan: milk is left to sour for about a day, then shaken in a gourd until the butter (fursa) separates, and the liquid left over is drunk as it is.

links.name: FAO, The technology of traditional milk products in developing countries

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Spare milk is seeded with the previous day's ferment, left overnight and churned at dawn; rob is the sour liquid left after the butter is taken off. Laban rayeb is the same ferment left unchurned.
